en: *The Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Eye of Mahāvairocana Buddha*,
recorded by the śramaṇa Ichigyō.
At that time, Acala Vidyārāja, grasping his sword of wisdom, manifested with fierce and wrathful majesty, and examined [the object].
Visualize clouds and dragons in the direction one is traveling;
by means of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sword Mudrā, sever and destroy them.
Those obstacles will immediately dissipate.
The reason for this is that when worldly people draw a maṇḍala upon an empty, open ground,
it is immediately destroyed if they encounter an evil dragon sending down rain.
It is likewise for the practitioner who draws the Maṇḍala of Great Compassion within the ground of the mind:
even if the evil dragons of the three poisons send down torrential rains and swift-flowing floods.
Because it causes inconceivable defilements to be submerged and obliterated,
he employs the body of stainless wisdom as the Vidyārāja Acala.
With his majestic and powerful might, he uses the mudrā of the sword of wisdom to sever and destroy the clouds of the aggregates (*skandha*).
Then, in whichever direction one turns, there will be nothing that is not clear and vast.
The "invoking sword" is the *kīla* (vajra-stake);
its head is like a single-pronged vajra.
The lower part is sharp and pointed,
like the shape of a stake;
if it is even more slender and minute, it is called a "vajra-needle."
Their characteristics are each distinct.
When the ācārya establishes the maṇḍala,
he may at times courageously establish the bodhicitta.
To pacify wind and rain by means of the *vajrakīla* ritual,
one should use *khadira* wood;
if that is unavailable, one may use *nimba* wood or even [a stake made of] tempered iron.
Empower yourself through the Vajrasattva of Accomplishing All Activities.
Visualize yourself as identical to all vajras,
and drive in the stakes to establish the boundaries of the directions.
Thereupon, cause all parts of the site for the practice of the Way to become identical with vajra;
thus, no obstacles will be able to cause affliction or harm.
Then, perform the mudrā of the union of Samādhi and Prajñā by joining the palms in the vajra gesture.
Bend the two index fingers with their tips pointing downward;
place each of the two thumbs beside the respective index fingers and press them down.
Place the mudrā at the heart and recite the mantra three times;
then disperse it over the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Next, one should visualize the wrathful and powerful Acala Vidyārāja dwelling in his position within the fundamental maṇḍala;
that is, a triangular maṇḍala surrounded by blazing flames.
That which is slightly black therein is this.
It is of two kinds:
either one visualizes the Noble Acala residing in his original position.
Trampling upon his crown with the feet of samādhi,
one may alternatively visualize oneself as Acala,
abiding in his original position.
Placing the feet of samādhi upon their heads and manifesting the majestic power of wrath,
all those who act as obstacles shall immediately retreat and disperse.
If one stubbornly refuses to follow these instructions and does not depart immediately,
they shall surely take their own life.
This is the mantra-holder.
One should give rise to a mind of compassion so as not to sever their life-force.
The reason for this is that such is the King of Immovables, the Pure Bodhicitta.
When the karma, afflictions, and lifespan that harm all sentient beings are extinguished,
one must immediately give rise to that life of the eternally true dharmatā;
thus, if the Buddhas cause practitioners to...
Those who would certainly fall into the nirvāṇa of annihilationism (uccheda-nirvāṇa) would incur the sin of killing sentient beings; therefore,
one should not adhere rigidly to the literal meaning of the text.
Thus, one loses the Tathāgata’s secret intention.
Next, the practitioner should enter the visualization of the Wrathful Trailokyavijaya Vidyārāja to purify the obstructions arising from oneself.
The two hands are crossed at the arms in vajra-fists;
the thumbs and index fingers hook together, and the middle and ring fingers are extended upward.
This is the method for entering into samādhi.
The practitioner then visualizes his own body emitting blazing flames,
with eight arms and four faces, baring sharp fangs.
The tiger’s roar of the syllable *HŪṂ* is like the sound of thunder;
it forms a boundary by circling clockwise upon the crown of the head.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ suṃbha ni suṃbha hūṃ | gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ | gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ | ānaya hoḥ | bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ. Immediately, he entered the *samādhi* of the Vajra Wrathful One, Blazing with Majestic Splendor, Victorious Over the Three Times.
The Bodhisattva has four faces, all of which are wrathful;
he has eight arms, each holding a weapon,
and his left foot treads upon Maheśvara.
The right foot treads upon the consort Umā,
standing in the *tiryag-pada* (T-shaped) posture.
His entire body blazes with flames, like the conflagration at the end of an eon.
This is precisely the samādhi-contemplation of the supreme noble ones of the three times.
A practitioner should abide in the arousal of the bodhicitta and give rise deeply to a mind of compassion,
thereby eliminating the obstructions of those within and without, as well as gods and humans.
Immediately, turning the seal three times counter-clockwise, one expels obstructing spirits;
then, turning it three times clockwise,
one binds the boundaries of the cardinal directions and intermediate points according to their desired size.
Then, seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head, reciting once at each location.
Perform the dispersal mudrā at the crown.
By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
Abiding in this wrathful samādhi,
all afflictions, karmic obstructions, and the like within body and mind are completely incinerated by the fiercely sharp fire of vajra-wisdom.
Next, perform the mudrā for protecting the body of the Vidyārāja Mañjuśrī:
interlace the two hands with the little fingers crossed within the palms;
then, double-bend the two ring fingers and insert them into the palms.
Place the two little fingers upon the crossed [fingers],
join the wrists, stand the middle fingers so that their tips touch one another,
and slightly bend the tips of the two index fingers.
Do not touch the back joint of the middle finger.
The mantra is: Oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ. Having recited this mantra seven times, [proceed].
If there is anyone who constantly desires to uphold the Vajra Dharma,
having washed their hands and face at dawn each day,
they should immediately cup pure water with their right hand and recite the mantra over it seven times.
Scatter [the offerings] toward the east three times.
Thereafter, enter the room and perform the rite for protecting the body.
As for the method of protecting the body:
Forming the mudrā without releasing it, recite the mantra aloud and seal the crown of the head;
next, seal the right shoulder.
Next, seal the left shoulder.
Next, seal the area before the heart.
Next, seal below the neck.
Next, seal the space between the eyebrows;
next, seal the hairline;
next, seal the crown of the head; having sealed the crown of the head, [seal] behind it.
This is the mudrā for this dharma.
Next is the mudrā of the Venerable Six-Limbed Wisdom King (Ṣaḍbhuja-jñānavajra):
form the inner vajra-bind with both hands.
The two middle fingers are held straight upright with their tips joined;
extend the two index fingers and slightly curve their bases so that they resemble three prongs.
The empowerment of the five places is the characteristic of this mudrā.
As for what are called the five places:
These are located at the forehead, the two shoulders, the heart,
and the throat. As for the two thumbs,
each right one presses down upon the left.
Then, insert [the fingers] into the moon. The mantra is:
Oṃ kṛt-ṣṭrī vikṛtānana hūṃ sarvaduṣṭān trāsaya stambhaya stambhaya svāhā svāhā hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Having bound this mudrā and recited this mantra, [proceed].
This refers to beginningless ignorance attaining mastery over all birth and death;
only the Vidyārāja of the Bodhicitta can subdue it,
even to the point of slaying that impermanent body.
This causes them to attain eternal life.
Other cases may be understood by inferring from this analogy.
Next, bind the mudrā of Vajrayakṣa Vidyārāja.
Form the inner vajra-bind with the hands of samādhi and wisdom;
join the tips of the two index fingers so that the space between them is like an eye.
With the two thumbs,
hold each index finger upright on its side so that they do not touch;
bend the first joints of each like a tusk.
Extend both little fingers slightly and bend their first joints together so that they face each other like two tusks.
Recite the mantra and empower the forehead, the two shoulders, the heart, and the throat.
Furthermore, open the five eyes;
that is to say, wipe the right and left eyebrows, the eyes, and the space between the eyebrows with the mudrā.
Seal the crown of the head and then release it. The mantra is:
Oṃ mahāyakṣa vajrasattva va ja hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ praveśaya hūṃ phaṭ. Having bound this mudrā and recited this mantra, [perform the rite].
If these various poisons are intended to act as obstacles,
one should apply them toward the image;
by treating it in this manner, those six sense faculties [will be purified].
It will immediately retreat and disperse like a fire being extinguished.
Next, bind the mudrā of Hayagrīva:
join the two hands in *añjali*.
The two index fingers and the two ring fingers are bent into the palms with their tips facing away from each other,
while both thumbs are held side by side.
Slightly bending [the body], do not touch the index finger;
then recite the mantra and circumambulate three times to the left to expel obstructing spirits.
Circumambulate three times to the right to establish the boundary.
The mantra is: Oṃ amṛtodanava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Form this mudrā and recite the mantra.
Medicines of pungent toxicity refer to the harsh antidotes such as impermanence, suffering, emptiness, non-self, and so forth.
It is like a disease that has deeply penetrated the heart and causes dizziness;
only by treating it can its root source be exhausted.
This applies even to Śakra, Brahmā, and the other kings of gods.
Possessing sovereign ease and happiness, he is the Honored One of the world.
The Tathāgata governs by means of this Dharma,
whereby one realizes that the mind and body are ablaze, like a destructive fire.
They feel weary of and terrified by birth and death,
and are correctly oriented toward nirvāṇa;
how much more so, then, for other sentient beings?
Next, bind the fundamental secret mudrā of the Invincible Vidyārāja.
Join the two hands with palms hollowed together;
align the tips of the ten fingers so that they touch and are held firmly closed.
This is the form of its mudrā.
The mantra is recorded elsewhere; because it is extremely secret, it is not transcribed here for the time being.
By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra, [the desired result is attained].
All obstacles are completely stilled,
so that none whatsoever can obscure or conceal the various instructions and commands of the Tathāgata’s true samaya.
Furthermore, with the palm of the left hand facing upward,
place the palm of the right hand face down upon it,
and using the thumb of the right hand...
Press the left thumb-nail;
snap the right index finger three times.
Next, bend and clench the four fingers from below the index finger of both hands.
Extend the thumb upright;
with the seal of the right hand,
rotate it counter-clockwise three times to perform the rite of expulsion.
Rotate it three times clockwise to establish the boundary.
Next, using the same mudrā,
point toward the four cardinal directions, the four corners, and the two directions of above and below.
One should then seal the five places of the body,
reciting the *hūṃ* mantra for each location to perform consecration.
Next, one binds the mudrā of the One-Syllable Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Vidyārāja.
Interlace the two hands within each other to form fists,
extend the two middle fingers,
and bend their upper joints into the shape of a sword.
Place the two thumbs side by side,
bend the two index fingers,
and pinch the upper joints of the two thumbs; this is it.
Empower the five places with the mudrā.
The mantra is: *Namo samantabuddhānāṃ bhrūṃ oṃ jyū*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the empowerment is accomplished].
All evil spirits shall not dare to approach this mantra-master;
they shall protect his own person and protect others as well.
The spirits summoned,
the spirits dispatched,
and the tasks sought to be accomplished.
Use this mantra in conjunction with it.
If the recitation of the mantra lacks divine efficacy,
recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
One will immediately achieve success regarding the attained realm;
if there is no efficacy, the deity will vanish.
Next, bind the mudrā of the consort Buddhalocanā.
For the mudrā, join the two hands in *añjali*,
bend the two index fingers,
and each rest them against the back of the middle finger.
Bend both thumbs inward into the palms.
Empower the five places with this seal and mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ ruru saphuru jvala tiṣṭha siddhalocane sarvaduṣṭān saṭṭani svāhā*. By forming this Buddhacakṣus mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
He causes the Lord of Secrets to extend this by applying it to all categories,
throughout all phenomena;
for this reason, it is called "Knowing the Three Mysteries."
He then cited the Buddha as witness, saying:
"For what reason?
The Blessed One is the samaya of all mantras."
This refers to abiding in one's own spiritual lineage (*gotra*).
For example, it is like a wheel-turning sage king (*cakravartin*);
if one abides within one's own spiritual lineage, [one attains such sovereignty].
By following and practicing the methods for governing the world as established by the wheel-turning kings of antiquity,
without adding or subtracting anything, the four quarters within his realm will naturally submit to his commands.
The World-Honored One is likewise so.
Because they always abide securely within the Tathāgata-gotra without transgressing it,
all the kings of mantras do not fail to act in accordance with the Dharma.
One regards this as the precept of the equality of nature and does not dare to transgress it.
Furthermore, it is like the four castes: the Kṣatriyas and Brāhmaṇas.
If one abides within their own spiritual lineage and honors its teachings,
they will be praised by the world and their endeavors will meet with success.
Now, this fundamental maṇḍala is likewise so.
Equanimous and immovable, it is the vajra-ground;
its nature is the nature of non-arising.
Perfect tranquility is the nature of the water of great compassion, which is beyond verbal expression.
Sharp illumination is the nature of the fire of wisdom, which is free from dust and defilement.
Expansion and contraction, formation and destruction, are the nature of the wind of self-existence, which is free from causes and conditions.
The image of signlessness is the nature of the great emptiness of the unconditioned void;
such is its nature that the Buddhas of the three times cannot create it.
How much less could those who create obstacles obscure it?
Therefore, bodhisattvas who practice the bodhisattva path through the gateway of mantras should likewise succeed to the lineage of the Tathāgatas.
One should emulate the various Honored Ones by abiding in their respective positions within the fundamental maṇḍala to perform all ritual activities.
If one wishes to perform the activity of pacifying calamities,
one should immediately manifest oneself as the body of the principal deity and abide within the circular maṇḍala.
If one performs rites of enrichment (*puṣṭi*),
one should abide within a square maṇḍala;
if one performs rites of subjugation (*abhicāra*) and so forth, [one should abide within a triangular maṇḍala].
One should abide in the triangular maṇḍala when wishing to perform the rite of summoning; one should abide in the crescent-shaped maṇḍala when wishing to perform the rite of attracting.
If one wishes to produce various kinds of adornments,
one should abide in the multicolored maṇḍala;
this can cause the practitioner to achieve realization such that they become identical with the deity.
Nothing that acts as an obstacle can obscure it.
Next, one contemplates the maṇḍala:
upon the center of an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Visualize variously adorned maṇḍalas;
upon these maṇḍalas, one should visualize the ocean-like assemblies of the three families.
Having performed this visualization, [proceed].
Then, forming the vajra-joined palms, one recites the verse:
By the power of my merit, The power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
And the power of the dharmadhātu, I universally make offerings to all the Honored Ones.
"I vow to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss, where I shall dwell making universal offerings.
Next, bind the seal of the Great Wheel Maṇḍala;
cover the left hand with the right.
Place it horizontally across the chest;
with the right hand turned upward,
rest it cumulatively upon the left hand.
The eight wheels are each interlaced with one another.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajracakra hūṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. Form this mudrā and recite the mantra;
place it before the heart and recite the mantra three times.
Then, facing downward, he presses the earth;
next, he seals the maṇḍala;
next, he seals the space above.
Next, seal the forehead;
next, seal the throat,
placing it only at the mouth.
At that time, one performs the "Sipping Seal" once;
as if in the motion of entering the mouth,
one then disperses it.
Next, observe the realms and paths.
First, form the five-pronged mudrā by joining the two palms together with the two water fingers and the two wind fingers.
Interlace the outer fingers of each hand;
place the two earth fingers and the two space fingers straight up, without touching one another.
The mudrā is formed by holding the two middle fingers upright like needles;
with this mudrā placed against the heart, one should visualize the maṇḍala.
Within the inner courtyard are boundary lines of five colors,
which adorn the perimeter.
Having performed this visualization, one should then visualize a white syllable *ra*.
Then, recite the syllable *ra* once and,
with the mudrā, circumambulate from the northeast corner to the right for one circuit.
Next, recite the syllable *raṃ*, which is red in color;
recite it once for each circuit as before.
Next, visualize the syllable *ka*, which is yellow in color.
Recite once and circumambulate once as above.
Next, visualize the letter MA, which is blue in color;
recite once and circumambulate once as above.
Next, visualize the black letter HA.
Recite it once around as before.
Then, recite the five-syllable mantra, saying:
*Namo samantabuddhānām raṅga*. Next, form the seal of summoning (*āhvāna-mudrā*): with both hands, perform the inner-binding (*antarbandha*);
extend the right index finger and slightly bend it like a hook.
Recite the mantra seven times. The mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ vaṃ*. Next, offer the argha water.
Form the añjali mudrā with the two hands;
the two vāyu fingers and the two ākāśa fingers are held upright and touching at their tips,
while the remaining fingers are spread apart and slightly bent.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ gaganasamāsama svāhā*. Next, perform the mudrā of the flower seat.
Performing the *argha* mudrā as previously described,
recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one attains the fulfillment of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*).
Next, form the incense-offering mudrā.
The five fingers of the right hand are held straight upright with the palm facing outward;
the left hand grasps the right wrist.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānām*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the obstacles are dispelled].
One attains the fulfillment of the Tathāgata’s fivefold untainted *dharmakāya*.
Next, one binds the Flower Mudrā:
with both hands, the eight fingers are interlaced within.
Open the palms facing upward;
with the two index fingers,
place them side by side against each other.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ niryūha*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
One attains the fulfillment of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded wisdom.
Next, form the incense mudrā:
turn both palms upward.
Expand the earth, water, and fire elements so that they adhere to one another's backs,
while the tips of the two wind elements buttress each other.
Placing the two *śūnyatā* [mudrās] alongside the wind-finger (*vāyu-aṅguli*),
recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one will swiftly attain the body of a Tathāgata, endowed with the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs of excellence.
Next, bind the food and drink mudrā:
extend both palms;
turn the right palm upward and place it over the left palm.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ pūrye*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the following occurs].
Having obtained the food of the joy of Dharma and the rapture of dhyāna,
next form the Lamp-Light Seal:
clench the left hand into a fist and place it at the waist.
The right hand likewise forms a fist;
extend the middle finger and hold it upright straight.
Recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ kṛyū*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one swiftly attains the five pure eyes of the Tathāgata.
Next, perform the vajra-joined palms (*vajra-añjali*) and recite the hymn of praise.
Extol the tutelary deity with the *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna*,
and then form the previously mentioned Buddha-eye mudrā (*buddhalocanā-mudrā*).
Recite the vidyā-mantra while consecrating the five places.
Next, form the mudrā for consecrating the rosary:
with both hands in the *candra-maṇḍala* (moon-disk) gesture, place the beads within.
Consecrate it seven times.
The mantra is: Oṃ vilokanāya svāhā. Next, hold the rosary with the right hand.
Place it within the left palm,
then place it within the joined palms,
and recite the mantra one thousand times.
Consecrate it seven times. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajrayakṣī-jāpasa-maye hūṃ. The practitioner enters samādhi and performs visualization.
Close the eyes and direct the mind,
focusing single-mindedly on a single object as one visualizes the deity,
neither too far nor too near.
With a mind of earnest devotion, recite the root mantra,
neither too hurried nor too slow, and neither too loud nor too low,
ensuring that the syllables and phrases of the mantra are precise.
Ensure that each part is clearly distinct.
Whether in three sessions or four sessions,
limit the recitation to one hundred and eight repetitions or one thousand and eighty.
When the recitation of the full number is completed,
perform the rite of offering;
thereafter, escort the principal deity and all the other deities back to their original palaces.
This is the most supreme and profoundly esoteric teaching;
do not forget it, and do not transmit it [to the unqualified].
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ muḥ svāhā.* The above is what was spoken by Vajrapāṇi;
the following is the description of the World-Honored One’s mudrās.
Thus it is, O Lord of Secrets, as you have said.
Furthermore, O Lord of Secrets,
regarding the description of the forms and characteristics of the various deities within the positions of the maṇḍala of all the noble ones:
One should know that it is likewise so;
this is what was taught by previous Buddhas,
and subsequent Buddhas further expanded upon its meaning.
As previously stated:
if any of the Honored Ones are described as yellow in color,
this signifies the vajra-colored body.
When it is within the wheel of the Indra direction,
if it is white, this is the color of naturally pure compassion.
When within the circular mandala,
if it is red in color,
this is the fierce color for the removal of obstacles.
When it is within a triangle,
if it is black, this is the color of the great winds of the kalpa-ending disaster.
Within the half-month,
if there is a blue color,
this is the indestructible and invincible color of space.
It refers to these wrathful vidyārājas and others,
who may be situated within a triangle or within a half-moon;
their colors and forms are likewise like those of the maṇḍala.
One should know that the physical appearance is likewise so: if it is yellow,
one should assume the expression of supreme progress and the joy of the Dharma.
If it is white, one should assume an expression of compassion and tranquil concentration; if it is red,
[one should assume an expression of wrath].
If [the practitioner] is of a dark complexion, they should assume a countenance of fierce and vigorous exertion. If [the practitioner] is of a black complexion,
they should assume a countenance of great power and swift momentum.
If it is blue, one should assume an expression that cannot be overcome; if it is yellowish-white,
[one should assume an expression that cannot be overcome].
This also serves to augment their majestic and formidable appearance.
By inferring from these examples,
one may understand even those of various mixed types.
One should simply distinguish and understand the nature and capacity of each matter as it arises;
even regarding that which has not been explicitly taught within the secret treasuries of all the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
One should likewise employ this same principle to initiate corresponding activities.
Therefore, the Buddhas of the past are cited as proof; for it is the natural law that they are universally applicable in the same way.
It is not that I alone have appeared in the world to speak thus;
those who practice yoga should understand the path of mental recitation.
When the recitation is completed:
Then, having performed the protection of the body, exit the hall.
Seal the Buddha and the stupa while simultaneously clarifying the yoga of the *iṣṭadevatā* (personal tutelary deity).
Thereafter, perform walking meditation as you please.
The Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Buddha-Eye of Mahāvairocana.
